subject: DPA: proof-of-deletion checklist & cross-border access playbook
messages:
From: Tilly Gomez <tilly@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-02-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA Qs — proof of deletion, backups & cross-border access

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the DPA draft. A few items the legal and security teams flagged that we need clarified / tightened before we can proceed:

1) Proof-of-deletion: What artefacts do you provide when we ask for deletion of a dataset or user? We need a stamped/certified artifact that shows the deletion run, timestamps, and the identifiers (snapshot IDs, storage object IDs).

2) Backups / snapshots: We understand backups may be immutable for some period. Can you confirm how long objects may remain in backups after a delete request and whether you can provide a remediation timeline for restoration & subsequent purge?

3) Cross-border access: Please confirm whether any developer/engineer access to EU/US-hosted data may occur outside the contracted geography for troubleshooting, and what controls/audit logs exist. Legal prefers any cross-border troubleshooting to be logged + notified within 48 hours.

4) Retention windows vs. on-demand erasure: We want a clear precedence rule if retention policies conflict with an erasure request (e.g., legal hold vs. data subject request).

5) Certification / attestation: Would Redwood be open to a quarterly attestation for erasure processes (summary report) and a one-time certified deletion for a specific dataset as a pilot?

Please send a short playbook you would provide as evidence for an erasure request, plus any proposed contract language. If easier, we can do a 30-minute call — we want to keep this moving this week.

Thanks,
Tilly Gomez
Senior Counsel, Acme Health

(attachment: acme-requested-redline.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tilly Gomez <tilly@acmehealth.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-01T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA Qs — proof of deletion, backups & cross-border access

Hi Tilly — thanks, really helpful list. High level answers below and I attached a concise playbook and a deletion-certificate template for your review. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through specifics.

Quick summary:
- Proof-of-deletion: We provide a deletion report that includes the deletion run id, timestamps, object identifiers (S3 keys / blob ids), and the job log. For model caches we include KV-cache purge markers and sequence hashes.
- Backups: For active customer data stored in our managed-hosted offering, snapshots are retained for disaster recovery for up to 30 days by default. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can discuss onshore-only backup windows and shorter snapshot retention (14 days).
- Cross-border access: Our standard practice is no routine cross-border developer access to customer region data. Emergency access follows an escalation playbook (ticket + approval from infra oncall) and is audited; we can add a 48-hour notification commitment.
- Retention vs erasure precedence: Legal holds will take precedence over service-level erasure requests; we will notify the requestor and provide the scope of the hold.
- Attestation: We can provide quarterly summary attestation reports, and we can run a one-time certified deletion for a pilot dataset (we'd issue an auditable deletion certificate).

Next steps I propose:
1) See attached: redwood-dpa-delete-playbook.pdf (summary playbook) and deletion-cert-template.docx.
2) Priyom (cc'd) will follow up with technical acceptance criteria we should bake into the DPA redline.
3) If that looks ok, we can drop in contract language and set a short call.

Would you be available for a 30 min call on Friday?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-dpa-delete-playbook.pdf)

Subject: Fwd: DPA Qs — proof of deletion, backups & cross-border access

Looping Rishi in for technical signoff. My read after talking to infra: we can meet most asks but need precise contract language so we're not committing impossible guarantees for immutable backups. Suggested redline points (technical acceptance criteria):

- "Proof artifacts" should be defined as: deletion-run id + timestamp + list of fully-qualified object identifiers + manifest of affected indexes + job-run logs (we can redact operational metadata on request).
- "Backup purge window": for hosted customers offer two options in the DPA: (A) standard hosted: 30-day backup retention with purge on request initiated at next backup cycle (we can provide snapshot IDs and purge confirmation within 7 business days after purge job runs); (B) Dedicated/Private: configurable down to 14 days with contract amendment.
- "Forensics & audit": deliverable to customer within 7 business days after purge completion: deletion_manifest.csv + machine-signed job log + snapshot IDs.
- "Cross-border troubleshooting": we can restrict interactive shell access; any ad-hoc access will require an oncall approval ticket, be time-limited, and produce an audit record. We can accept a 48-hour notification SLA on any ad-hoc access.

Notes: we cannot guarantee immediate removal from long-term immutable cold archives if the customer has requested extended archival settings — those must be handled via a separate archival purge agreement.

Attaching a technical playbook draft for the legal redline (technical-delete-playbook.md).

- Priyom

Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA Qs — proof of deletion, backups & cross-border access

Thanks — everything here looks reasonable. A couple of pragmatic concessions I'd propose for the DPA redline so we don't over-promise: 

1) Backup purge SLA: we should offer "purge confirmation within 7 business days after purge job runs" but also explicitly call out that purge execution may happen on the next snapshot cycle and can therefore be up to 30 days from request for standard hosted. For Dedicated/Private, offer a 14-day max.

2) For the proof artifact, add that we will provide machine-signed logs and snapshot IDs; we cannot always provide raw disk-level proofs for multi-tenant hardware — we'll provide the highest-fidelity logical artifacts available.

3) Certified deletion pilot: agree, but add that certified deletion will include a joint acceptance checklist signed by both parties and is limited to a single dataset per certification event.

4) Annual third-party attestation: we can offer an annual SOC-style attestation covering deletion processes for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private plans.

I'll also propose a short paragraph to add to the redline around "legal hold vs erasure" precedence: legal holds will suspend erasure timelines but we will provide immediate notification and an estimated hold duration.

- Rishi

Hi Tilly — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal review (Priyom and Rishi cc'd) we've consolidated a pragmatic redline package that balances your requirements with operational constraints. Attached: redwood-dpa-redline-proposal.docx (contains exact DPA language and an appendix with the deletion artifact format). Also attached: technical-delete-playbook.md and deletion-cert-template.docx.

Highlights from the redline:
- Proof-of-deletion: Redwood will deliver a deletion_manifest.csv (object ids + snapshot ids), a machine-signed job log, and a deletion-run certificate.
- Backup purge timing: Standard hosted = up to 30 days due to snapshot cycles; purge confirmation (post-purge) within 7 business days. Dedicated/Private = configurable to 14 days.
- Cross-border troubleshooting: Any ad-hoc access will be time-limited, ticketed, and Redwood will notify Acme within 48 hours with the audit packet.
- Legal hold vs erasure: Legal hold supersedes erasure; Redwood will notify the requestor and provide hold scope & estimated duration.
- Attestation: Quarterly summary attestation reports available; annual third-party attestation offered for Dedicated/Private customers.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please review the attached redline and the deletion_cert template.
2) If acceptable, we can convert the redline into a short amendment and circulate for signature — I can host a 30-minute call to walk the legal/security team through the artifacts.
